core_obligations: Identify the class of the diagonal (proof lines 1757-1775): the pullback along the diagonal is the cup product, and the class of the diagonal is the pushforward of the fundamental class; the latter is idempotent under the intersection product, hence its cycle class is either zero or one in the one dimensional coefficient algebra of the variety, and it cannot be zero because pairing it with the class of a closed point does not vanish.

Compute the pairings (proof lines 1775-1799): pairing the class of the diagonal with a product of classes gives the pairing of the two classes on the variety; expanding the Kunneth decomposition of the class of the diagonal and using the behaviour of the degree map under products turns this into a sum of products of pairings against the components; choosing one class so that it pairs to one with a fixed component and to zero with all others identifies the complementary component, which yields the displayed orthogonality with the sign.
proof_roadmap: Identify the class of the diagonal with the pushforward of the unit and compute its canonical basis expression.
Pair the decomposition with a product of classes using the product formula for the degree map.
Choose a dual class to read off the asserted pairings.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a classical Weil cohomology theory the Kunneth components of the class of the diagonal of a smooth projective variety pair to plus or minus the Kronecker symbol (statement lines 1752-1765). The proof (proof lines 1766-1799) identifies the class of the diagonal as the pushforward of the unit, expands its Kunneth decomposition, and computes the pairings through the product formula for the degree map. H3: a computation with an explicit choice of dual class, written out in full.
